scenes.headline: The King of the Road
scenes.sub: How a war surplus Jeep became a Filipino icon
scenes.voiceover: They call it the King of the Road. Loud, colourful, and packed with passengers. This is the jeepney.

scenes.headline: Born from leftover Jeeps
scenes.sub: US military Jeeps stayed behind after World War Two
scenes.voiceover: After World War Two, American military Jeeps were left behind in the Philippines. Filipinos stretched them, added benches, and turned them into public transport.

scenes.headline: Every one is decorated
scenes.sub: Chrome horses, paint, names and prayers
scenes.purpose: Why it looks the way it does.
scenes.voiceover: Owners made each one their own. Chrome horses on the hood, bright paint, family names and prayers across the front.

scenes.headline: Bayad po!
scenes.sub: Passing your fare down the line
scenes.voiceover: Riding one has its own rules. You hand your fare to the person beside you, say bayad po, and it travels hand to hand to the driver.

scenes.headline: PUV Modernization begins
scenes.sub: A push to replace old jeepneys with newer vehicles
scenes.voiceover: In 2017, the government launched the PUV Modernization Program, aiming to replace ageing jeepneys with cleaner, newer vehicles.

scenes.headline: Ride one while you can
scenes.purpose: Payoff with a gentle call to action.
scenes.voiceover: The classic jeepney is changing fast. So next time one stops for you, hop on and enjoy the ride.
